title: Charles's path from hidden momentum to pure electrostatic thrust (2010 forces, 2018 realization)

tellings.quote:
where in 2010 I saw the forces initially
could have been something else but
that's where I started and it wasn't
until after two years working with Drew
I said oh Drew's got the he's got the
conversion down from field momentum um
to mechanical momentum without static
charges. My wife pointed that out and uh
so we did the test. So for two years we
thought that's what the case. It wasn't
until 2018 where I realized that I
didn't even need the current.

plain: A researcher who goes by Charles says that in 2010 he first saw unexplained forces in his lab, and that working with a colleague named Drew he came to think the push came from "hidden momentum," an idea that momentum stored in electric and magnetic fields can turn into ordinary motion. He says that in 2018 he realized he did not even need the electric current, only static charge, to get thrust. If true, it would point to a way of moving a craft without fuel or propellant.
